cases.finding: The exact-named Bursa Governorship page has been located by publisher and title, but its full text remains unverified. The 1326–1364 claim is not independently established, and no replacement chronology or Source attachment is proposed.

cases.original_publication: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Art of the Timurid Period (ca. 1370–1507)
cases.original_locator: Essay opening paragraph (Timur made Samarqand his capital in 1370; Timur's death in 1405)
cases.original_access: Metropolitan Museum original publisher essay directly indexed and corroborated; old October review had ORIGINAL_REVIEWED_PARTIAL_SUPPORT because interval through 1405 was not yet independently corroborated.

additional_evidence.locator: COURTS AND COURTIERS V: Timurid and Turkman dynasties, discussion of the proposed capital at Kesh versus Samarqand and its status by Timur's death in 1405
additional_evidence.supports: Independent specialist historical article supports Samarqand as the capital selected by Timur and a major capital at his death in 1405.

additional_evidence.locator: Timeline: Timurid {1370–1506}, opening passage and succession to Shah Rukh after Timur's 1405 death
additional_evidence.supports: Supports Timur's 1370 Samarkand control and 1405 death, and a later imperial court governed by Shah Rukh from Herat. Does not justify claiming Samarkand was the sole Timurid capital for 1370–1507.

cases.finding: Source-supported narrow claim: Timur established his capital at Samarqand in 1370 and the city remained his imperial capital up to his death in 1405. The reviewed original 1370–1405 interval is acceptable only when defined as capital of Timur's personal reign (inclusive terminal year), not proof of uninterrupted exclusive capital status for the full Timurid dynasty after 1405. Separate subsequent rulers and rival courts. Historic fact/Source support advanced; canonical identity and source-ID status are not approval to write.
